title: Ride tram 28 through the Alfama
description: A 1930s wooden Remodelado grinding up the hills through the old Moorish quarter. Board at Martim Moniz early or you will stand.

title: Eat a pastel de nata where they were invented
description: The monks' recipe went to the bakery next door in 1837 and has not left the family since. Cinnamon on top, eaten warm, standing up.

title: Watch the sunset from a Lisbon miradouro
description: The highest of the city's viewpoints, with the castle, the river and the bridge all in one frame and a fraction of the crowd.

title: Hear fado in a small Alfama house
description: Two guitars and one voice, and the room goes silent when it starts. The tourist dinner shows are not the same thing.

title: Stand at the westernmost point of Europe
description: A cliff 140 metres above the Atlantic where the mainland runs out. Camoes called it the place where the land ends and the sea begins.

title: See the Joanina library in Coimbra
description: A baroque library that keeps a colony of bats to eat the insects that would otherwise eat the books. They are let out at night.

title: Walk to the Covao dos Conchos funnel
description: A perfectly circular spillway swallowing a lake into a tunnel, built in 1955 and looking entirely unnatural.

title: Cross the top deck of the Dom Luis I bridge
description: Designed by a student of Eiffel. The upper deck carries the metro and a footway 60 metres above the Douro.

title: Taste port in a Vila Nova de Gaia lodge
description: Every big port house has its cellars on the south bank. A tawny tasting flight explains more than any amount of reading.

title: Swim in the lagoons of Peneda-Geres
description: Portugal's only national park, with granite plunge pools, Roman milestones and wild garrano ponies in the hills.

title: Look inside the chapel of bones at Evora
description: Five thousand monks' bones set into the walls by friars making a point about mortality, with the point written over the door.

title: Stargaze on the Alqueva dark sky reserve
description: The world's first certified starlight tourism destination, over Europe's largest artificial lake.

title: Watch the Atlantic from Cabo de Sao Vicente
description: Where Henry the Navigator sent his ships out into the unknown. The lighthouse has one of the strongest beams in Europe.

title: Walk the Rota Vicentina fishermen's trail
description: A path along the cliff edge on sand, used by fishermen to reach their spots. Harder than it looks and far emptier than the south coast.

title: Walk a levada through the laurel forest
description: Irrigation channels cut into the cliffs from the 1500s, with footpaths beside them running into a UNESCO laurisilva forest.

title: Stand on the glass floor at Cabo Girao
description: The highest cliff skywalk in Europe, 580 metres straight down to terraced smallholdings on the shoreline.

title: Look down into the Sete Cidades crater
description: Twin lakes, one green and one blue, in a volcanic caldera. The Vista do Rei viewpoint is the classic, weather permitting.

title: Cook a stew in volcanic ground at Furnas
description: Cozido buried in the hot earth for six hours beside the fumaroles, then dug up at noon and served in the village.

title: Climb Pico, the highest point in Portugal
description: Two thousand three hundred and fifty-one metres of volcano straight out of the Atlantic. Registration and a tracker are compulsory.

title: See the Book of Kells at Trinity
description: A ninth-century gospel book, then the Long Room above it with two hundred thousand volumes on oak shelves.

title: Walk the Howth cliff loop
description: A headland at the end of the DART line, with a six-kilometre cliff path, seals in the harbour and puffins on Ireland's Eye.

title: Drink a pint where it was brewed
description: Seven floors up a giant glass pint, ending in a bar with a 360-degree view of the city. Learn to pour one on the way.

title: Stand inside Newgrange
description: A passage tomb from 3200 BC, older than the pyramids, built so the winter solstice sun runs down the passage to the chamber.

title: Drive the Slea Head loop
description: Beehive huts, a fifteen-hundred-year-old oratory and the Blasket Islands offshore, on a single-track road you drive clockwise.

title: Cycle the Gap of Dunloe
description: A glacial pass between the Purple Mountain and Macgillycuddy's Reeks, with a boat back across the Killarney lakes.

title: Walk the Slieve League cliffs
description: Six hundred metres, nearly three times the Cliffs of Moher, and with a fraction of the visitors. The One Man's Pass is the exposed bit.

title: Walk the Gobbins cliff path
description: An Edwardian path of bridges and tunnels bolted onto a basalt sea cliff, reopened in 2015 after eighty years derelict.

title: Walk the limestone pavement of the Burren
description: A hundred and fifty square kilometres of bare karst where Arctic, alpine and Mediterranean plants grow side by side in the cracks.

title: Take the cable car to Dursey Island
description: Ireland's only cable car, crossing a sound where the water rips through, to an island with no shop and almost no people.

title: Cycle the Great Western Greenway
description: Forty-two kilometres of traffic-free path on an old railway from Westport out to Achill Sound.

title: Climb Benbulben's flat top
description: A limestone table cut by glaciers, with Yeats buried in its shadow at Drumcliffe under his own epitaph.

title: Swim in the Limmat at a Zurich badi
description: The city swims in its own river. The Flussbad Oberer Letten lets you drift 400 metres downstream and climb out at the end.

title: Watch the Zytglogge clock strike
description: An astronomical clock from 1530 with a parade of bears four minutes before the hour. Einstein lived along the same street.

title: Ride the train up to the Jungfraujoch
description: Europe's highest railway station at 3,454 metres, through a tunnel inside the Eiger, onto the Aletsch ice.

title: Walk the Eiger Trail under the north face
description: Six kilometres directly beneath the 1,800-metre north wall, from Eigergletscher down to Alpiglen. Rockfall is audible.

title: See the Matterhorn from the Gornergrat
description: A cog railway to 3,089 metres facing the mountain, with twenty-nine four-thousand-metre peaks visible from the terrace.

title: Walk the larch forests of the Engadin in autumn
description: Larch is a conifer that turns gold and drops its needles. For two weeks in October the whole valley goes copper.

title: Swim in the Verzasca river
description: Water clear enough to look fake, over smooth grey and white rock. The dam upstream is the one Bond jumps off.

title: Cross the Chapel Bridge in Lucerne
description: A covered wooden bridge from 1333 with painted panels in the roof beams, rebuilt after a fire in 1993.

title: Ride the Gotthard Panorama Express
description: A paddle steamer across Lake Lucerne then a train up the old Gotthard line, which loops through the mountain three times.

title: Stand for a night at the Staatsoper
description: Standing tickets go on sale eighty minutes before curtain for a few euros. Tie a scarf to the rail to keep your place.

title: Sit all afternoon over one coffee
description: The Viennese coffee house is UNESCO-listed as an intangible tradition, and nobody will ask you to leave.

title: See the Klimt kiss at the Belvedere
description: The world's largest Klimt collection in a baroque palace, with the gold-leaf painting everyone comes for in one small room.

title: Go inside the Eisriesenwelt ice caves
description: The largest ice cave in the world, forty-two kilometres long. You carry a carbide lamp and climb 700 steps in the cold.

title: Tour the Hohensalzburg fortress
description: One of the largest fully preserved castles in Europe, never taken in nine hundred years, on a rock above Mozart's town.

title: Ride the Nordkette cable car from the old town
description: Twenty minutes from a medieval street to 2,256 metres, on a line with stations designed by Zaha Hadid.

title: Meet the Otztal glacier road
description: The highest paved road in Austria, running to 2,830 metres on a glacier that hosts the first World Cup ski race each October.

title: Climb the Schlossberg clock tower steps
description: Two hundred and sixty steps up a hill in the middle of Graz, to a clock tower whose hands are the wrong way round.

title: Swim in the Worthersee
description: An alpine lake that reaches 26 degrees in summer, warm enough to swim in without flinching, ringed by wooden bathhouses.

title: See the Night Watch at the Rijksmuseum
description: Rembrandt's militia painting, restored in public view behind glass. The library and the Asian pavilion are the quiet corners.

title: Book months ahead for the Anne Frank House
description: The annexe behind the bookcase, kept unfurnished at Otto Frank's request. Tickets release six weeks out and go in minutes.

title: See working windmills at Zaanse Schans
description: Industrial windmills still sawing timber and grinding pigment, moved here to be saved rather than built as a display.

title: Cycle the bulb fields around Keukenhof
description: Seven million bulbs planted every year, open only for eight weeks. The fields outside the gardens are free and just as good.

title: Sit on the wharf cellars in Utrecht
description: A canal with its quays a full storey below street level, the old goods cellars now cafes at the waterline.

title: Take the ferry to Terschelling
description: One of the Wadden islands, thirty kilometres of empty North Sea beach, cranberry fields and more bicycles than cars.

title: Drive the Delta Works storm barrier
description: Nine kilometres of barrier built after the 1953 flood, with sixty-two gates that close when the North Sea rises three metres.

title: Stand in the Grand-Place at night
description: Guild houses in gold leaf around a square Victor Hugo called the most beautiful in the world. Floodlit after dark.

title: Eat frites from a friture with the right sauce
description: Twice-fried in beef fat, in a paper cone, with one of about twenty sauces. Belgians will fight you over the choice.

title: Climb the Belfry of Bruges
description: Three hundred and sixty-six narrow steps to a carillon of forty-seven bells over a canal town that stopped growing in 1500.

title: See the Ghent Altarpiece after its restoration
description: Van Eyck's 1432 polyptych, the most stolen artwork in history, with one panel still missing since 1934.

title: Look at diamonds and Rubens in Antwerp
description: Eighty per cent of the world's rough diamonds pass through four streets here, next to the house Rubens built for himself.

title: Hear the Last Post at the Menin Gate
description: Buglers have sounded it every evening at eight since 1928, apart from the German occupation. Fifty-four thousand names with no known grave.

title: Walk the Ardennes at Durbuy
description: Billed as the smallest city in the world, on a bend in the Ourthe, with wooded hills and the Battle of the Bulge ground beyond.

title: Ride a boat lift on the Canal du Centre
description: Four Victorian hydraulic boat lifts still working, and a modern one that raises barges seventy-three metres in one go.

title: Walk the Bock casemates
description: Twenty-three kilometres of tunnel cut into the rock under the city, which sheltered thousands during the world wars.

title: Walk the Mullerthal Trail
description: Sandstone clefts, moss and ladders through what the country calls its Little Switzerland, an hour from the capital.

title: Take the chairlift above Vianden castle
description: A restored feudal castle on a spur over the Our valley, with an open chairlift up the hill opposite for the view back.
